What does Playwright check before a click (actionability)?
a: The element is attached, visible, stable (not animating), enabled and receives events (not covered). It retries until these pass or it times out.

q: fill vs pressSequentially: when do you use each?
a: fill: almost always (fast, replaces the value). pressSequentially: when the page reacts to each key (autocomplete, filter-as-you-type, input masks).

q: Call log: 'waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable - element is not enabled'. Fix?
a: The element is disabled. Do the step that enables it first (check a box, fill required fields). Don't add waits or force: true.

q: Why must page.once('dialog', ...) come BEFORE the click?
a: Without a listener Playwright dismisses dialogs automatically. If you register it after the click, the dialog was already dismissed.

q: Why start page.waitForEvent('popup') before the click, but await it after?
a: Awaiting before the click would wait forever (the click never runs). Starting after the click could miss the event. So: start the Promise, click, then await.
